2607.25633.title: Construction-Driven Injection: Linguistically-Grounded Edit-Based Code-Mixing Fingerprints for Large Language Models
2607.25633.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are costly intellectual assets that remain exposed to unauthorized redistribution and commercial misuse. Injected fingerprints, i.e., trigger--target pairs embedded in model behavior, offer a practical, black-box-verifiable ownership signal, but existing methods decouple the two stages of the fingerprint life cycle: how a fingerprint is constructed and how it is injected. Existing fingerprinting frameworks suffer from two limitations. Natural-language fingerprints are prone to accidental activation, and garbled fingerprints are easily filtered by perplexity-based detection. Furthermore, decoupling construction from injection leaves the latter unaware of the trigger's linguistic structure, missing the opportunity for targeted optimization. We argue that fingerprint construction should drive injection, and present a unified fingerprinting framework that jointly optimizes both stages. First, LCF constructs code-mixing fingerprints by combining low-resource languages under a semantic-density substitution rule and grammar-biased mixing, yielding triggers whose perplexity sits far below garbled baselines while avoiding the accidental-activation failures of natural-language triggers. Second, LCFEdit injects each fingerprint with a null-space projection derived from high-resource multilingual representations that preserves knowledge, augmented by a cross-lingual alignment step that steers the weight update toward the fingerprint language's representation subspace. This construction-aware injection ensures that the update is linguistically informed and therefore more stable. Extensive evaluations on imperceptibility, detectability, and harmlessness demonstrate persistent ownership verification with negligible impact on utility.
2607.25633.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）是昂貴的智力資產，仍然面臨未經授權的再分配和商業濫用的風險。注入的指紋，即嵌入模型行為中的觸發--目標對，提供了一種實用的、黑箱可驗證的所有權信號，但現有方法將指紋生命週期的兩個階段解耦：指紋是如何構建的以及如何被注入。現有的指紋框架存在兩個限制。自然語言指紋容易意外激活，而混亂的指紋則容易被基於困惑度的檢測過濾。此外，將構建與注入解耦使得後者無法了解觸發的語言結構，錯失了針對優化的機會。我們主張指紋的構建應該驅動注入，並提出一個統一的指紋框架，聯合優化這兩個階段。首先，LCF通過在語義密度替代規則和語法偏向混合下結合低資源語言來構建代碼混合指紋，產生的觸發其困惑度遠低於混亂的基線，同時避免了自然語言觸發的意外激活失敗。其次，LCFEdit通過從高資源多語言表示中派生的零空間投影注入每個指紋，這保留了知識，並通過跨語言對齊步驟增強，將權重更新引導至指紋語言的表示子空間。這種考慮構建的注入確保了更新是語言上知情的，因此更穩定。在不可察覺性、可檢測性和無害性方面的廣泛評估顯示，持續的所有權驗證對效用的影響微乎其微。
